sections.title: 选词填空
paragraphs: Travel websites have been around since the 1990s, when Expedia, Travelocity, and other holiday booking sites were launched, allowing travelers to compare flight and hotel prices with the click of a mouse. With information no longer[[26]]by travel agents or hidden in business networks, the travel industry was revolutionized, as greater transparency helped [[27]] prices. Today, the industry is going through a new revolution—this time transforming service quality. Online rating platforms— [[28]] in hotels, restaurants, apartments, and taxis—allow travelers to exchange reviews and experiences for all to see. Hospitality businesses are now ranked, analyzed, and compared not by industry [[29]], but by the very people for whom the service is intended—the customer. This has [[30]] a new relationship between buyer and seller. Customers have always voted with their feet; they can now explain their decision to anyone who is interested. As a result, businesses are much more [[31]], often in very specific ways, which creates powerful [[32]] to improve service. Although some readers might not care for gossipy reports of unfriendly bellboys(行李员)in Berlin or malfunctioning hotel hairdryers in Houston, the true power of online reviews lies not just in the individual stories, but in the websites’ [[33]] to aggregate a large volume of ratings. The impact cannot be [[34]]. Businesses that attract top ratings can enjoy rapid growth, as new customers are attracted by good reviews and [[35]] provide yet more positive feedback. So great is the influence of online ratings that many companies now hire digital reputation managers to ensure a favorable online identity.

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation: C) controlled 语法判断:空格前是Withinformationnolonger,空格后是by引出的介词短语,由此可知,此处是 “with+宾语+宾语补足语"结构,本句中information是宾语,由后面的by可知宾语补足语应该是一个过 去分词短语,即空格处应填入一个过去分词。符合语法条件的过去分词选项有controlled(控制)、forged (锻造,塑造;形成)和overstated(过分强调;夸大)。 语义判断:由下文orhiddeninbusinessnetworks可知,所填入词应与hidden呈并列关系,且由空格前 的with结构的中心词information和下文的greatertransparency可知,此处是说“信息受到控制”,将符 合语法条件的备选项代入文中可知controlled符合文意,为答案。 ·2015年6月六级真题(第三套)·

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation: L) slash 语法判断:空格前为helped,空格后为prices,可知空格处应填入一个动词原形,构成help(to)dosth. 的结构。符合语法条件的备选项有entail(使必需;导致)和slash(大幅度削减)。 语义判断:本句前半部分提到,随着信息不再受旅行社控制,或不再隐匿于商业网站,旅游业发生了 革命性的改变,由此可知,此处是说更强的透明度帮助“大幅度削减了”价格,动词原形slash符合文 意,为答案。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation: M) specializing 语法判断:空格前为破折号,空格后为介词短语inhotels,restaurants,apartments,andtaxis,可知空格处 应填入分词,与介词in一起构成分词短语,修饰破折号前面的platforms。或者也可以填入形容词,作 platforms的后置定语。符合语法条件的备选分词还有forged、overstated、persisting(坚持)和specializing (专于),形容词有accountable(负责任的)和pessimistic(悲观的)。 语义判断:前文提到,如今,这一行业正在经历一场新的变革一—这次是服务质量的变革,由此可知, 本句是说专门针对酒店、餐馆、公寓和出租车的在线评级平台能够让出行者互相交流意见和各自的体 验,符合语法条件的备选项中specializing与in一起构成specializein这一短语,意为“专于;专攻;专 营",符合此处语境,故本题答案为specializing。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation: K)professionals 语法判断:空格前为notbyindustry,空格后有butbytheverypeople,由此可以判断,此处使用了not.. but..结构,意思是“不是而是..",因而空格处应填入一个名词作by的宾语。符合语法条件的名 调选项有capacity(能力;容量)、incentives(刺激,鼓励)、professionals(专业人士)和spectators(观众)。 语义判断:上一段结尾提到了在线评级平台能够让人们相互交流意见和经验,由此可知,本段是阐述 这种在线评级体制的具体特点,由本句中的not.but..结构可知,notbyindustry 与butbythe verypeople并列,又由后面破折号引出的thecustomer可知,theverypeople具体指的就是the customer,可见“industry ”应该与thecustomer呈对应关系。结合备选名词选项含义可知, professionals(专业人士)符合文中语境,industryprofessionals即“行业专业人士”,与thecustomer(顾客) 对应,故本题答案为professionals

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation: E) forged 语法判断:空格前为Thishas,空格后为anewrelationshipbetweenbuyerand seller,由此可以判断,空 格处应填入一个过去分词,与has一起构成现在完成时,充当谓语。符合语法条件的备选过去分词还有 forged 和 overstated。 语义判断:上文提到,目前是由顾客而不是行业专业人士为服务商家评级,可知本句是说这种转变显

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation: A)accountable 语法判断:空格前为businessesaremuchmore,空格后为逐号,可知空格处应填入多音节形容词,与 more一起构成比较级,充当主系表句型中的表语。符合条件的形容词有accountable和pessimistic。 语义判断:前文提到,顾客总是能够自由选择,他们现在可以向任何感兴趣的人解释自己的决定,可 知本句是说顾客此种行为的结果,即商家变得更加负责,备选项中accountable符合文意,故为答案。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.explanation: F) incentives 语法判断:本空位于一个which引导的定语从句中,空格前为whichcreatespowerful,空格后为to improveservice,可知定语从句中缺少谓语creates的宾语,故应填入一个名词。符合语法条件的备选名 词还有capacity、incentives和spectators。 语义判断:前文提到,商家变得更加负责任,由此可知,此处是说,这为改善服务质量创造了强大的 “激励机制”,备选名调中incentives意为“刺激,鼓励”,符合语境,故为答案。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.explanation: B) capacity 语法判断:空格前为butinthewebsites,空格后为toaggregatealargevolumeofratings,由此可知,空 格处应填入名词。符合语法条件的备选名词还有capacity和spectators。 语义判断:本句中也使用了not..but...结构,由此可知,与notjustintheindividual stories(不仅仅存在于 个人评论之中)相对应的应该是“还在于网站可以积聚大量评论的能力”,capacity意为“能力;容量”, 符合文意,故为答案。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.explanation: H)overstated 语法判断:空格前为Theimpactcannotbe,空格后为句点,由此可知,空格处应填入形容词或过去分 词,充当主系表句型中的表语,符合语法条件的备选项还有overstated和pessimistic。 ·2015年6月六级真题(第三套)· 语义判断:上段末尾提到,网络评论真正的威力不仅仅存在于个人评论之中,还在于网站可以积聚大 量评论的能力。由此可知,本段开头句承上启下,说的应该是在线评论的影响力问题,将备选项代入文 中,overstated符合上下文语境,故为答案。cannotbeoverstated意为“再怎么强调都不过分”。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.explanation: O) subsequently 语法判断:空格前为asnewcustomersareattractedbygood reviews and,空格后为provideyetmore positivefeedback,可知空格位于由as引导的原因状语从句中,areattracted和provide构成并列谓语, 故provide前面缺少一个修饰性的副词。符合语法条件的副词有occasionally(偶然地)和subsequently (随后,后来)。 语义判断:“好评会吸引新的顾客”和“新的顾客给出更加积极的反馈"有时间上的先后承接关系,故 subsequently符合文中语境,为答案。

sections.title: 长篇匹配
paragraphs: A) A thin magnetic stripe (magstripe) is all that stands between your credit-card information and the bad guys. And they’ve been working hard to break in. That’s why 2014 is shaping up as a major showdown: banks, law enforcement and technology companies are all trying to stop a network of hackers who are succeeding in stealing account numbers, names, email addresses and other crucial data used in identity theft. More than 100 million accounts at Target, Neiman Marcus and Michaels stores were affected in some way during the most recent attacks, starting last November.

B) Swipe(刷卡)is the operative word: cards are increasingly vulnerable to attacks when you make purchases in a store. In several recent incidents, hackers have been able to obtain massive information of credit-debit-(借记)or prepaid-card numbers using malware, i.e. malicious software, inserted secretly into the retailers’ point-of-sale system—the checkout registers. Hackers then sold the data to a second group of criminals operating in shadowy corners of the web. Not long after, the stolen data was showing up on fake cards and being used for online purchases.

C) The solution could cost as little as $2 extra for every piece of plastic issued. The fix is a security technology used heavily outside the U.S. While American credit cards use the 40-year-old magstripe technology to process transactions, much of the rest of the world uses smarter cards with a technology called EMV (short for Europay, MasterCard, Visa) that employs a chip embedded in the card plus a customer PIN (personal identification number) to authenticate(验证)every transaction on the spot. If a purchaser fails to punch in the correct PIN at the checkout, the transaction gets rejected. (Online purchases can be made by setting up a separate transaction code.

D) Why haven’t big banks adopted the more secure technology? When it comes to mailing out new credit cards, it’s all about relative costs, says David Robertson, who runs the Nilson Report, an industry newsletter. “The cost of the card, putting the sticker on it, coding the account number and expiration date, embossing(凸印)it, the small envelope—all put together, you’re in the dollar range. ” A chip- and-PIN card currently costs closer to $3, says Robertson, because of the price of chips. (Once large issuers convert together, the chip costs should drop.

E) Multiply $3 by the more than 5 billion magstripe credit and prepaid cards in circulation in the U.S. Then consider that there’s an estimated $12.4 billion in card fraud on a global basis, says Robertson. With 44% of that in the U.S. American credit-card fraud amounts to about $5.5 billion annually. Card issuers have so far calculated that absorbing the liability for even big hacks like the Target one is still cheaper than replacing all that plastic.

F) That leaves American retailers pretty much alone the world over in relying on magstripe technology to charge purchases—and leaves consumers vulnerable. Each magstripe has three tracks of information, explains payments security expert Jeremy Gumbley, the chief technology officer of Credit Call, an electronic-payments company. The first and third are used by the bank or card issuer. Your vital account information lives on the second track, which hackers try to capture. “Malware is scanning through the memory in real time and looking for data,” he says. “It creates a text file that gets stolen.”

G) Chip-and-PIN cards, by contrast, make fake cards or skimming impossible because the information that gets scanned is encrypted(加密). The historical reason the U.S. has stuck with magstripe, ironically enough, is once superior technology. Our cheap, ultra-reliable wired networks made credit- card authentication over the phone frictionless. In France, card companies created EMV in part because the telephone monopoly was so maddeningly inefficient and expensive. The EMV solution allowed transactions to be verified locally and securely.

H) Some big banks, like Wells Fargo, are now offering to convert your magstripe card to a chip-and-PIN model. (It’s actually a hybrid(混合体)that will still have a magstripe, since most U.S. merchants don’t have EMV terminals.) Should you take them up on it? If you travel internationally, the answer is yes.

I) Keep in mind, too, that credit cards typically have better liability protection than debit cards. If someone uses your credit card fraudulently(欺诈性的),it’s the issuer or merchant, not you, that takes the hit. Debit cards have different liability limits depending on the bank and the events surrounding any fraud. “If it’s available, the logical thing is to get a chip-and-PIN card from your bank,” says Eric Adamowsky, a co-founder of Credit Cardlnsider.com. “I would use credit cards over debit cards because of liability issues.” Cash still works pretty well too.

J) Retailers and banks stand to benefit from the lower fraud levels of chip-and-PIN cards but have been reluctant for years to invest in the new infrastructure (基础设施)needed for the technology, especially if consumers don’t have access to it. It’s a chicken-and-egg problem: no one wants to spend the money on upgraded point-of-sale systems that can read the chip cards if shoppers aren’t carrying them—yet there’s little point in consumers’ carrying the fancy plastic if stores aren’t equipped to use them. (An earlier effort by Target to move to chip and PIN never gained progress.) According to Gumbley, there’s a “you-first mentality. The logjam(僵局)has to be broken.”

K) JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon recently expressed his willingness to do so, noting that banks and merchants have spent the past decade suing each other over interchange fees—the percentage of the transaction price they keep—rather than deal with the growing hacking problem. Chase offers a chip- enabled card under its own brand and several others for travel-related companies such as British Airways and Ritz-Carlton.

L) The Target and Neiman hacks have also changed the cost calculation: although retailers have been reluctant to spend the $6.75 billion that Capgemini consultants estimate it will take to convert all their registers to be chip-and-PIN-compatible, the potential liability they now face is dramatically greater. Target has been hit with class actions from hacked consumers. “It’s the ultimate nightmare,” a retail executive from a well-known chain admitted to TIME.

M) The card-payment companies MasterCard and Visa are pushing hard for change. The two firms have warned all parties in the transaction chain—merchant, network, bank—that if they don’t become EMV-compliant by October 2015, the party that is least compliant will bear the fraud risk.

N) In the meantime, app-equipped smartphones and digital wallets—all of which can use EMV technology—are beginning to make inroads(侵染)on cards and cash. PayPal, for instance, is testing an app that lets you use your mobile phone to pay on the fly at local merchants—without surrendering any card information to them. And further down the road is biometric authentication, which could be encrypted with, say, a fingerprint.

O) Credit and debit cards, though, are going to be with us for the foreseeable future, and so are hackers, if we stick with magstripe technology. “It seems crazy to me,” says Gumbley, who is English, “that a cutting-edge-technology country is depending on a 40-year-old technology.” That’s why it may be up to consumers to move the needle on chip and PIN. Says Robertson: “ When you get the consumer into a position of worry and inconvenience, that’s where the rubber hits the road.”

questions.stem: It is best to use an EMV card for international travel.
questions.explanation: H 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词EMV和international travel。文中C段、G段、H段、M段和N段都出 现了EMV这个词,因此可以将答案锁定在这几个段落。但只有H段提到了出国旅行,最后一句提到 If youtravelintermnationally,theansweris yes,也就是说,如果你要出国旅行,应该办理一张芯片加密卡。 原文中的travel intermationally与题干中的intermationaltravel表意相同。

questions.stem: Personal information on credit and debit cards is increasingly vulnerable to hacking.
questions.explanation: B 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词increasinglyvulnerableto hacking。文中B段提到,当你在商店购物时, 银行卡越来越容易受到攻击。黑客利用悉意软件窃取大量消费者的信用卡、借记卡和预付卡的卡号信 息,换言之就是消费者信用卡和借记卡的个人信息越来越容易受到黑客的攻击。因此答案为B。

questions.stem: The French card companies adopted EMV technology partly because of inefficient telephone service.
questions.explanation: G 解析:根据题干中的关键词Frenchcardcompanies和inefficienttelephoneservice定位到G段。G段倒数 第二句提到,在法国,信用卡企业开发EMV的一部分原因就在于,电话行业的垫断导致该过程(通过 电话无障碍地进行信用卡认证)效率极其低下,而且资费更是高得离谱。因此题是对原文的同义转 述。题干中的partlybecauseof对应原文中的inpartbecause;inefficient是原词复现。

questions.stem: While many countries use the smarter EMV cards, the U.S. still clings to its old magstripe technology.
questions.explanation: C 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词manycountriesusethesmarterEMVcards和oldmagstripetechnology。 文中论及很多国家使用更智能的信用卡及其与美国的对比的内容是在C段。C段第三句提到,当美国 的信用卡还在使用40年前的磁条技术来处理交易时,世界上的其他很多国家则使用了更加智能的卡 ·2015年6月六级真题(第三套)· 片。这句话刚好是对题干的同义转述。原文中的muchoftherestoftheworld对应题干中的many countries;原文中的the40-year-old对应题干中的its old。

questions.stem: Attempts are being made to prevent hackers from carrying out identity theft.
questions.explanation: A 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词attempts arebeingmade和preventhackersfromcarryingoutidentity theft。文中提到人们正在努力阻止黑客盗用他人身份的只有A段,该段第三句提到了银行、执法部门 和技术公司一致努力,试图挫败一个盗用他人身份的黑客网络。题干是对原文的同义转述,因此答案 为A。题干中的attempts arebeingmade对应原文中的arealltryingto;identitytheft是原词复现。

questions.stem: Credit cards are much safer to use than debit cards.
questions.explanation: I 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词creditcards aremuch safer。文中把信用卡和借记卡的安全性相比较的 只有I段。I段首句说信用卡通常比借记卡的责任保护性更强,最后埃里克·阿达莫夫斯基所说的话也 体现了这两者的对比:“考虑到责任承担问题,我会更倾向于使用信用卡,而不是借记卡。”因此使用信 用卡比使用借记卡要安全得多,题干是对原文的同义概括。题干中的aremuchsafertouse对应原文中 的 have better liability protection。

questions.stem: Big banks have been reluctant to switch to more secure technology because of the higher costs involved.
questions.explanation: D 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词bigbanks、reluctant、moresecuretechnology和highercosts。文中论及大 型银行不愿意转用更加安全的技术的内容是在D段。D段首句即提出疑问:为什么大银行尚未采用这 种更加安全的技术呢?之后引用戴维·罗伯逊的话该到这完全是出于成本考虑。因此题干是对原文的同 义概括,其中switchto对应原文中的adopted,becauseofthehighercosts involved对应原文中的it'sall about relative costs。

questions.stem: The potential liability for retailers using magstripe is far more costly than upgrading their registers.
questions.explanation: L 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词potentialliability和farmorecostlythanupgradingtheiregisters。文中L 段提到了potential liability。本段谈到,凯捷集团的顾问们预计将所有用户的卡片全部升级为芯片加密 卡将会花掉约67.5亿美元。尽管零售商们不愿意花费这笔钱,然而他们现在所面临的潜在债务正在激 增。题干正是对这两句话的概述,其中isfarmorecostly对应原文中的isdramaticallygreater。

questions.stem: The use of magstripe cards by American retailers leaves consumers exposed to the risks of losing account information.
questions.explanation: F 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词Americanretailers、consumers和losingaccountinformation。文中论及美 国零售商使用磁条卡使消费者面临风险的是F段。该段第一句谈到,美国零售商成为了世界上为数不 多的依赖磁条收费技术的零售商,这使得消费者更容易受到伤害。后面解释了受到的伤害是个人账号 信息可能被黑客盗取。故题干是对原文的同义概括。

questions.stem: Consumers will be a driving force behind the conversion from magstripe to EMV technology.
questions.explanation: O 解析:注意抓住题干中的关键词consumerswill beadrivingforce。文中提到消费者的推动作用的是O 段,该段倒数第二句说,这就是为什么可能还是得由消费者们来推动磁卡向芯片加密卡升级了。故题 干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的consumerswillbeadrivingforce对应原文中的itmaybeupto consumers to move the needle。

sections.title: 仔细阅读 · 1
paragraphs: What’s the one word of advice a well-meaning professional would give to a recent college graduate? China? India? Brazil? How about trade? When the Commerce Department reported last week that the trade deficit in June approached $50 billion, it set off a new round of economic doomsaying. Imports, which soared to $200.3 billion in the month, are subtracted in the calculation of gross domestic product. The larger the trade deficit,the smaller the GDP. Should such imbalances continue, pessimists say, they could contribute to slower growth. But there's another way of looking at the trade data.Over the past two years, the figures on imports and exports seem not to signal a double-dip recession--a renewed decline in the broad level of economic activity in the United States-but an economic expansion. The rising volume of trade—more goods and services shuttling in and out of the United States—is good news for many sectors. Companies engaged in shipping, trucking,rail freight,delivery, and logistics(物流) have all been reporting better than expected results. The rising numbers signify growing vitality in foreign market—when we import more stuff, it puts more cash in the hands of people around the world, and U.S. exports are rising because more foreigners have the ability to buy the things we produce and market. The rising tide of trade is also good news for people who work in trade-sensitive businesses, especially those that produce commodities for which global demand sets the price-agricultural goods, mining, metals, oil. And while exports always seem to lag, U.S. companies are becoming more involved in the global economy with each passing month.General Motors sells as many cars in China as in America each month. While that may not do much for imports, it does help GM's balance sheet—and hence makes the jobs of U.S.-based executives more stable. One great challenge for the U.S. economy is slack domestic consumer demand.Americans are paying down debt, saving more, and spending more carefully. That's to be expected, given what we've been through. But there’s a bigger challenge. Can U.S.-based businesses,large and small, figure out how to get a piece of growing global demand? Unless you want to pick up and move to India, or Brazil, or China, the best way to do that is through trade. It may seem obvious, but it's no longer enough simply to do business with our friends and neighbors here at home. Companies and individuals who don't have a strategy to export more,or to get more involved in foreign markets, or to play a role in global trade, are shutting themselves out of the lion’s share of economic opportunity in our world.

questions.stem: How do pessimists interpret the U,S. trade deficit in June?

options.text: It reflects Americans' preference for imported goods.
It signifies a change in American economic structure.
It could lead to slower growth of the national economy.
It is the result of America's growing focus on domestic market.

questions.explanation: C 定位:根据题干中的信息词pessimists和tradedeficit,可以把答题线索定位到第二段末句。 解析:题干问的是悲观主义者对六月份美国贸易赤字的看法。第二段末句提到:“悲观主义者说,如果 提到了“只与国内的朋友和邻居做生意是天经地义的事”,但不能说明美国人越来越注重国内市场, 而是目前出口处境艰难,且这并不是悲观人士的观点,故排除选项D。选项A和选项B在原文中均未 提及。

questions.stem: What does the author say about the trade data of the past two years?

options.text: It indicates that economic activities in the U.S. have increased.
It signals decreasing domestic demand for goods and services.
It reflects the fluctuations in the international market.
It shows that U.S. economy is slipping further into recession.

questions.explanation: A 定位:根据题干中的信息词tradedata和thepasttwoyears,可以把答题线索定位到第三段第二句。 解析:第三段第二句提到:“过去两年来,进口和出口的有关数据似乎并不能表明经济在经历二次衰退 (即美国经济活动大范围的再次衰遥),而是表明经济在扩张。”由此可知,作者认为贸易数据是经济扩 张的表现,故答案为A,并排除选项D。文中提及进口猛增,贸易赤字加大,但这并不能说明对商品和 服务的国内需求减少,构不成因果关系,故排除B。选项C属于中性的观点,但作者在文中并未提及这 一观点,也可排除。

questions.stem: Who particularly benefit from the rising volume of trade?

options.text: People who have expertise in international trade.
Consumers who favor imported goods and services.
Producers of agricultural goods and raw materials.
Retailers dealing in foreign goods and services.

questions.explanation: C 定位:根据题干中的信息词particularlybenefit和risingvolumeoftrade,可以把答题线索定位到第四段 末句。题干中的particularly与文中的especially对应,而risingvolumeoftrade与risingtideoftrade对应。 解析:题干问谁从增加的贸易量中获益最多。第四段末句提到:“贸易的增长趋势对那些在贸易敏感行 业工作的人,尤其对那些产品价格由全球需求决定(农产品、矿产、金属和石油)的生产商来说,同样是 好消息。”由此可知,上述四种产品的生产商在贸易量增加中受益最为明显,选项C中用rawmaterials (原材料)同义替换了原文的mining,metals,oil(矿产、金属和石油),故答案为C。选项A、B、D在文中 都未提及,均可排除。

questions.stem: What is one of the challenges facing the American economy?
questions.explanation: .C 定位:根据题干中的信息调oneofthechallenges和Americaneconomy,可以把答题线索定位到第六段 首句。 解析:题干问的是美国经济面临的一个挑战是什么。文章第六段首句提到:“美国经济的一个重大挑战 在于国内消费需求的萎靡。”接着第二句又说:“美国民众都在偿还货款,他们把更多的钱用于储蓄,消 费也更加谨慎。”由此可知国内消费需求不旺,即人们不愿意花钱,故答案为C。注意:由于文中出现了 slack容易误选D,但D项说的是萎靡的贸易活动,明显不符合文意。选项A、B两项都没有在文中提 到,故可排除。

questions.stem: What is the author's advice to U.S. companies and individuals?

options.text: To import more cheap goods from developing countries.
To increase their market share overseas.
To be alert to fluctuations in foreign markets.
To move their companies to where labor is cheaper.

questions.explanation: B 定位:根据题干中的信息调companiesandindividuals以及题文同序的原则,可以把答题线索定位到 末段。 解析:末段提到:“任何公司和个人,如果不采取策略扩大出口,不更多地参与到国外市场上来,不在 ·2015年6月六级真题(第三套)· 全球贸易中发挥作用的话,都将与全球经济中的大部分机遇无缘。”不难看出作者建议美国公司和个人更 多地参与国际贸易,扩大其在海外市场上的份额,因此答案为B。选项A、C和D在原文中均未提及。

sections.title: 仔细阅读 · 2
paragraphs: A recurring criticism of the UK's university sector is its perceived weakness in translating new knowledge into new products and services. Recently, the UK National Stem Cell Network warned the UK could lose its place among the world leaders in stem cell research unless adequate funding and legislation could be assured.We should take this concern seriously as universities are key in the national innovation system. However, we do have to challenge the unthinking complaint that the sector does not do enough in taking ideas to market.The most recent comparative data on the performance of universities and research institutions in Australia, Canada,USA and UK shows that, from a relatively weak starting position, the UK now leads on many indicators of commercialisation activity. When viewed at the national level, the policy interventions of the past decade have helped transform the performance of U.K. universities.Evidence suggests the UK’s position is much stronger than in the recent past and is still showing improvement.But national data masks the very large variation in the performance of individual universities. The evidence shows that a large number of universities have fallen off the back of the pack, a few perform strongly and the rest chase the leaders. This type of uneven distribution is not peculiar to the U.K. and is mirrored across other economies. In the UK, research is concentrated: less than 25% of universities receive 75% of the research funding. These same universities are also the institutions producing the greatest share of PhD graduate, science citations, patents and licence income. The effect of policies generating long-term resource concentration has also created a distinctive set of universities which are research-led and commercially active. It seems clear that the concentration of research and commercialisation work creates differences between universities. The core objective for universities which are research-led must be to maximise the impact of their research efforts. These universities should be generating the widest range of social, economic and environmental benefits. In return for the scale. of investment,they should share their expertise in order to build greater confidence in the sector. Part of the economic recovery of the UK will be driven by the next generation of research commercialisations pilling out of our universities. There are three dozen universities in the UK which are actively engaged in advanced research training and commercialisation work. If there was a greater coordination of technology transfer offices within regions and a simultaneous investment in the scale and functions of our graduate schools, universities could, and should, play a key role in positioning the U.K. for the next growth cycle.

questions.stem: What does the author think of UK universities in terms of commercialisation?

options.text: They still have a place among the world leaders.
They have lost their leading position in many ways.
They do not regard it as their responsibility.
They fail to convert knowledge into money.

questions.explanation: A 定位:根据题干关键词commercialisation可以将答案定位至文章第三段第二句。 解析:本题问作者认为英国大学在商业化方面做得如何。该段第二句指出:“针对澳大利亚、加拿大、 美国和英国的大学和研究机构的表现的最新比较数据显示,虽然英国的起点相对较低,但现在英国已 经在很多商业化活动的指标中居于世界领先地位。”由此可见作者认为英国大学在商业化方面在世界 上仍然处于领先地位,故选A。

questions.stem: What does the author say about the national data on UK universities’ performance in commercialisation?

options.text: It masks the fatal weaknesses of government policy.
It does not reflect the differences among universities.
It does not rank UK universities in a scientific way.
It indicates their ineffective use of government resources.

questions.explanation: B 定位:根据题干关键词thenationaldata可以将答案定位至文章第四段最后两句。 解析:第四段第三句和第四句指出:“但是全国性的数据掩盖了不同大学在表现上的巨大差异。有证据 表明很大一部分大学已经落后了,少数大学表现良好,而剩下的都在追赶。”由此可知,全国性数据并 不能反映出各个大学间的不同,故选B。

questions.stem: We can infer from Paragraph 5 that “policy interventions”(Line 1, Para. 4) refers to .

options.text: concentration of resources in a limited number of universities
compulsory cooperation between universities and industries
fair distribution of funding for universities and research institutions

questions.explanation: A 定位:根据题干中的Paragraph5和policyinterventions可以迅速将答案定位至文章第五段。 解析:本题考查的是policyinterventions在句中的含义,该词组出现在第四段,但第四段并没有详细论 述它的含义。因此要理解这个调组需要到后文找答案,即第五段。第五段第二句指出:“在英国,研究很 ·2015年6月六级真题(第三套)· 集中:不到25%的大学获得了75%的研究经费。”由此可以得出,policyinterventions在句中的含义是国 家将研究经费投入到数量有限的大学中去,即资源集中在数量有限的大学,故选A。

questions.stem: What does the author suggest research-led universities do?

options.text: Fully utilise their research to benefit all sectors of society.
Generously share their facilities with those short of funds.
Publicise their research to win international recognition.
Spread their influence among top research institutions.

questions.explanation: A 定位:题干信息词research-led最先出现在文章第五段,但是本题所考查内容在第五段没有出现。而文 章第六段再次出现了research-led,可知答案在第六段。 解析:第六段第二句指出:“这些大学应该创造出最广泛的社会效益、经济效益和环境效益。”与选项A 表述一致,故选A。

questions.stem: How can the university sector play a key role in the UK’s economic growth?

options.text: By establishing more regional technology transfer offices.
By asking the government to invest in technology transfer research.
By promoting technology transfer and graduate school education.
By increasing the efficiency of technology transfer agencies.

questions.explanation: C 定位:根据题干信息词playakeyrole可以将答案定位于文章最后一段。 解析:文章最后一段提到:“如果能够更好地协调各个地区的技术转让办公室,同时给研究生院投资以 扩大规模和改善功能,大学或许并且应该能够在下一轮增长中为巩固英国的地位发挥关键作用。”由 此可知,促进技术转让和加强研究生教育能使大学在巩固英国的地位中发挥关键作用,故选C。
